name: Aqueduct of Padre Tembleque Hydraulic System
description: This 16th-century aqueduct stretches across the high plateau between the states of Mexico and Hidalgo, carrying spring water over roughly 45 kilometres of canals, tanks and arched bridges. Its showpiece is a towering single-tier arcade, the tallest ever built in an aqueduct. Franciscan friar Padre Tembleque began it, and local indigenous communities built it, blending Roman engineering with Mesoamerican adobe techniques.
